description: This working note studies the three-defect isotropic heading-refresh substrate of SFIT Part V. It proves an averaged completed-block stability estimate for an isolated interrupted relaxation: the probability that the total signed over/under crossing reward differs from the ballistic reference is bounded by Cq[1 + log(1/q)]. The proof combines longitudinal anti-concentration for independent uniform headings, the chord lemma for repeated-defect renewals, and an oriented-area sign analysis for overlapping motion of different defects. The estimate establishes absolute convergence of isolated single-insertion response integrals and an O(r^2) Beta-law correction; it does not establish differentiability of the full stationary Green–Kubo coefficient. The note formulates the adjacent two-gap mixed response, identifies the residual displacement proportional to uv, and states the unproved adjacent-stability, higher-cluster, and stationary-limit estimates needed for a full small-r expansion theorem. A separate event-driven v2 primary test of the candidate second-order crossing-count coefficient, nu_2 = 3.222716 (numerical integration SE 0.025403), agrees with a fresh-seed extrapolated estimate 3.2301 (statistical SE 0.0404), with a prespecified decision statistic z = 0.15 (PASS). This is coefficient-level numerical validation under the stated decision rule, not a proof of the full stationary expansion. The second-order Green–Kubo coefficient Gamma_2 remains a numerical candidate.
